(3) Not a power wall: the same shapes sustained for 60 s in standalone cuBLAS hold 97.3 TFLOPS at 1432 MHz / 243 W (cap 300 W), no throttling. why: measured from the shape histogram instrumentation plus the existing nsys trace; kernel-overlap test is a pure sqlite interval query over CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_KERNEL for device 0; sustained cuBLAS test is /tmp/gemm_sustain.cu

why: single-card sustained test was already on record at 97.3 TFLOPS; this round adds the 4-card concurrent run to rule out system-level power/thermal capping, which was the last untested hypothesis after kernel selection, call fragmentation and the FLOPs accounting were all resolved

decision: Overlap feasibility resolved for the prefill all-reduce. (1) The AR is link-limited, not latency-limited: 6656 all-reduce kernels on device 0 are 6131 in a narrow 5.2-5.9 ms band (508 small <1 ms ones are decode), and one 41.9 MB AR at 5.4 ms is busbw 11.64 GB/s = 93% of practical PCIe3 x16 (~12.5 GB/s). So there is nothing to win by splitting/re-tuning NCCL itself. (2) But the AR kernel uses only 2 blocks (~2 SMs of 80) while Kernel2 uses 1813 blocks, so compute and communication do not contend for resources. (3) The current zero overlap is therefore pure same-stream ordering: all NCCL and all GEMM run on the single cudaStreamPerThread. (4) Ceiling for hiding: min(GEMM 39.2 s, AR 36.3 s) = up to 36.3 s, i.e. 104.2 -> 67.9 s (-35%), now backed by the 93% link figure plus the 2-SM occupancy plus the measured zero overlap. Risk to check when implementing: overlapping may slow the AR (SMs and PCIe shared), so the real hidden fraction needs an A/B. Implementation points located: FastllmNcclAllReduceImpl (fastllm-multicuda.cu:3099) submits on cudaStreamPerThread, and the row-parallel TP pattern is DoCudaLinear -> DoCudaLinear -> FastllmNcclAllReduce (multicudadevice.cpp:3670-3691).
why: AR bandwidth derived from the measured kernel duration distribution in /home/nsys/pf180k.sqlite (device 0); occupancy from grid/block dims in the same trace; the -35% ceiling is arithmetic on the two measured device-0 budgets

decision: All-reduce/GEMM overlap feasibility measured directly, and the -35% ceiling from the previous round is corrected down. Probe: 4 GPUs in one process (thread-per-device, like the engine), GEMM cublas M=8704 N=4096 K=5120 (fp16, tensor op) against an NCCL half all-reduce of 41.9 MB (4096x5120, exactly the engine's prefill message). Results, repeated 3x each: (a) AR enqueued on a side stream from the SAME host thread as GEMM: GEMM-alone 373 ms, AR-alone 557 ms, both 775 ms => only 27-28% of the AR hides. (b) AR issued from a DEDICATED host thread: GEMM-alone 373-376 ms, AR-alone 555-560 ms, both 542-569 ms => 65-72% of the AR hides. So whether the overlap works depends on the NCCL host proxy having its own progress thread, not on which stream is used. Also learned: NCCL collectives on this box hang unless each device has its own host thread (a single-threaded 4-device loop deadlocks in ncclAllReduce even though ncclCommInitAll succeeds) -- the engine already uses thread-per-device ops, so it is compatible. Corrected ceiling: hiding ~2/3 of the 36.3 s AR saves about 24 s, 104.2 -> ~80 s (-23%), not the -35% printed in the plan
why: thread-per-device probe matching the engine's structure; both variants repeated 3 times with stable results; the 41.9 MB AR reproduces the engine's measured 5.4-5.6 ms per call, confirming the probe models the real message

decision: Dependency-chain overlap measured, and it caps the win far below the independent-case number. The engine's row-parallel pattern is GEMM -> all-reduce -> next GEMM, i.e. the AR consumes the GEMM that just ran, so no amount of buffering removes the dependency. Probe (4 GPUs, thread-per-device, GEMM 8704x4096x5120 vs 41.9 MB AR), 40 layers, repeated 3x with stable results: (A) AR per layer with force-sync (warmup semantics) 366.7/367.0/368.9 ms; (C) the engine's actual steady shape -- AR enqueued on the SAME main stream, no per-layer sync -- 365.3/365.6/365.9 ms, i.e. within 1% of fully serial, confirming today's zero overlap; (B) AR on a SIDE stream, no per-layer sync -- 309.2/309.3/310.4 ms = 16% hidden; (D) two AR buffers on a side stream with the AR submitted one layer ahead (a real 1-deep pipeline) -- 308.3/311.0/311.0 ms, no better than (B). So under the engine's real dependency chain the ceiling is ~16%, not the 65-72% measured for independent GEMM/AR, and not the -23% derived from it. Moving the AR to a side stream alone captures essentially all of it; a deeper pipeline buys nothing because the chain is dependency-bound
why: the independent-case probe from the previous round had no data dependency between GEMM and AR, which is why it showed 65-72%; adding the dependency (AR consumes its GEMM's output, next GEMM consumes the AR) drops the ceiling to 16% and makes double-buffering useless. Variant C reproduces the engine's steady state (force-sync is only active during warmup; basellm.cpp:4094 only clears it for arch>=75, so on SM70 the steady state is 'enqueued on the same stream without per-layer host sync')

decision: Legal split-based overlap measured with the dependency preserved, and it recovers nearly all of the previous round's (illegal) number. Design: split the row-parallel output into nsplit pieces; GEMM(c) on the main stream, an event, then AR(c) on a side stream that waits that event, so AR(c) runs concurrently with GEMM(c+1); the layer ends by joining both streams. This keeps the data dependency (each AR waits its own GEMM, the next layer waits both) unlike the previous round's variant B/D which did not chain the AR back. Results at 30 layers, 4 GPUs, thread-per-device, repeated: nsplit=1 -> 1.2%; 2 -> 1.2%; 4 -> 8.7%; 6 -> 14.4%; 8 -> 14.2/14.4/14.9% (stable); 12 -> 13.6%; 16 -> 7.7% (fragments too small, GEMM efficiency drops); 32 crashed the probe (event array overflow in the harness, not the engine). So the sweet spot is nsplit=8 giving ~14-15% of the layer time, essentially the same as the 16% from the dependency-free variant, but now via a legal schedule. Practical read for the 104.2 s prefill: ~14% of the 36.3 s AR ~= 5 s, i.e. wall ~99 s, close to the -6% in the plan
why: unlike the previous round's B/D variants, every AR here waits its own GEMM via cudaStreamWaitEvent, so the number already excludes illegal reordering. The optimum is a genuine trade-off: more splits hide more AR but shrink the GEMMs, and by nsplit=16 the GEMM efficiency loss cancels the gain

decision: Why the overlap ceiling does not transfer to the engine: the engine runs at queue depth 1 (one kernel in flight per device at all times), so there is no execution substrate for concurrency. Direct measurement from /home/nsys/pf180k.sqlite device 0: 1077724 kernels, max_concurrent_kernels_on_device = 1, and the time with >=2 kernels in flight is 0.00 s. Host side agrees: 60854 cudaStreamSynchronize calls spread evenly across the whole 118 s run, blocking each of the 4 worker threads for 97 s of 118 s (82%), while device 0 is kernel-busy 108.5 s -- host-blocked time tracks GPU-busy time, the signature of submit-wait-submit. The syncs attribute to whatever kernel preceded them (16953 after Kernel2, 8523 after the NCCL all-reduce, 7370 after volta_h884gemm_64x64, ...), i.e. they are per-op, not one-off. Consequence for the objective: the 14% measured by the split probe assumed the host submits all work up front and only synchronizes at the end; the engine submits and waits op by op, so moving the AR to a side stream cannot overlap anything until the queue depth is raised. A real implementation therefore needs BOTH a side stream AND batching/queuing changes (submit the layer's ops without intermediate host waits), which is a much larger change than the plan's current 'two streams' framing
why: kernel concurrency computed by a sweep-line over the device-0 kernel intervals; host sync count and blocked time from CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_RUNTIME; sync attribution by nearest preceding kernel end

decision: CORRECTION to plan item 4b (reduce-scatter + all-gather 'halves the traffic'): it does not. For an activation of S elements across n ranks, ring all-reduce moves 2(n-1)/n*S per rank and reduce-scatter + all-gather moves (n-1)/n*S in each of its two phases, i.e. exactly the same total. Measured on this box with the engine's prefill message size (S = 4096x5120 fp16 = 41.94 MB, 4 ranks, thread-per-device, 50 reps): all-reduce 5.567 ms vs RS+AG 5.874 ms, ratio 1.06, so RS+AG is ~6% slower rather than 2x faster. The 'traffic halves' premise would only hold for something like the all-gather-only portion of a sequence-parallel scheme, not for replacing all-reduce with RS+AG
why: ring volume arithmetic plus a direct measurement; the RS+AG scheme that does reduce traffic needs sequence parallelism (sharding the activations so each phase only moves S/n), which is a different and much larger refactor than what 4b described

decision: CORRECTION to my own round-5 mechanism claim. I attributed the engine's host lockstep to ForceDeviceSync (cudaDeviceSynchronize) on the per-op path, but the trace says otherwise: cudaDeviceSynchronize is only 4483 calls / 0.54 s total, while the 388 s of host-blocked time is 60854 cudaStreamSynchronize calls (0.11 s total host time in cudaStreamWaitEvent, 80619 calls). Nor is it a per-kernel lockstep: only 3% of those syncs waited on exactly 1 kernel, 11% on 6-7 kernels, so it is operator-granularity. Only 5.8% of the syncs begin within 0.1 ms after an all-reduce kernel ends, so NCCL post-sync is not the driver either. The syncs are spread evenly across the whole run (~3.5-6k per 10 s bucket).
why: kernel-concurrency, runtime-API and wait-window analyses are all over /home/nsys/pf180k.sqlite; the earlier conclusion (queue depth 1 is real, measured as max_concurrent=1 on all four devices) stands, but its cause is operator-granularity stream synchronisation in the MultiCuda dispatch path, not the device-sync I named

decision: The engine already ships an async dispatch path that avoids the per-op synchronisation, gated by a flag that Qwen3.5 never enables. In fastllm-multicudadevice.cpp, multiCudaPersistentAsyncDispatch (thread_local, default false, multicudadevice.cpp:41, setter at :527) selects RunMultiCudaDeviceOps -> SubmitOrderedMultiCudaDeviceOps/WaitMultiCudaDeviceOps, which hand off between the caller stream and persistent per-device worker streams with events (completion event waited via FastllmCudaCurrentThreadStreamWaitEvent) instead of the ForceDeviceSync used by the fallback RunMultiCudaDeviceOpsOnTemporaryThreads. Grep shows MultiCudaSetPersistentAsyncDispatch(true) is called only from src/models/deepseekv4.cpp (six sites, for graph launch / sampling / TP async), never from qwen3_5.cpp. So raising the queue depth for Qwen3.5 may be a small wiring change (enable the existing path for its prefill), not the 'host execution-model refactor' I wrote in round 5
why: grep of the setter's callers; code read of both dispatch branches. Not yet measured for Qwen3.5: enabling it may change numerics or break assumptions (dependencies are preserved by events, but the Qwen3.5 path has extra streams/scratch), so it needs an A/B with a sha256 check

decision: Measured the engine's existing async dispatch path on Qwen3.5 via a new opt-in env gate (FASTLLM_MULTICUDA_ASYNC_DISPATCH, default off, wiring only -- no call-site changes). It engages: cudaStreamSynchronize drops from 60854 calls / 388.1 s to 6926 calls / 32.5 s (-92% host blocking), with the token sha256 unchanged (adcb1bd7) and Total time flat (3.2162 s off vs 3.2196 s on, 8K prompt). But device-side concurrency is still 1: max_concurrent kernels is 1 on all four devices in both arms, and 8K wall time does not move. So the async path removes host waiting without creating any GPU-side overlap -- proof that host blocking was NOT what prevented overlap. Raising the queue depth is therefore necessary but nowhere near sufficient: the dispatch still enqueues onto one stream per device, so communication and compute still cannot run together
why: the flag demonstrably changes the runtime API profile yet leaves max_concurrent=1 on every device and the wall time unchanged, which separates 'host waits' from 'device cannot overlap' as two independent facts

decision: CORRECTION to what I told the user about item 2 (sequence parallelism): I wrote that RS + all-gather moves 0.938S per rank vs 1.500S for all-reduce, i.e. 62%. That is wrong -- I divided by n twice in the all-gather term. Correct ring volumes for n=4: all-reduce 2(n-1)/n*S = 1.500S; reduce-scatter (n-1)/n*S = 0.750S; all-gather (n-1)/n*S = 0.750S. RS+AG together = 1.500S, byte-for-byte the same volume as all-reduce. This matches my own round-4 measurement (RS+AG 5.874 ms vs AR 5.567 ms, 6% slower). Sequence parallelism therefore does NOT reduce communication volume by itself; what it buys is that the norm only runs on the local 1/n shard, which is a compute saving, not a communication one
why: recomputed the ring collective volumes; the earlier claim came from writing the all-gather term as (S/n)*(n-1)/n

decision: Measured the ceiling of item 1 (fuse all-reduce + residual + RMSNorm) on OUR workload instead of borrowing 1Cat's number. On the 180K prefill trace (device 0), inside the prefill window bounded by the 5.6 ms all-reduces (113.6 s): FastllmAddToKernel 7551 calls / 1.068 s plus all RMSNorm kernels 11101 calls / 0.931 s = 2.00 s = 1.76% of the window. The engine ALREADY has a fused all-reduce+residual path (FastllmTryTP2P2PAllReduceAdd, used via Qwen3CudaTryTP2P2PAllReduceAddResidual in qwen3_5.cpp at 5606/11336/12675/29882/30109), and 92% of the 5.6 ms all-reduces are immediately followed by FastllmRMSNormHalfVirtual1024Kernel (6096 of 6656). So the remaining prize for item 1 is only the norm pass that could be folded in, i.e. roughly 0.9 s of 113.6 s = 0.8%, not the 3.5% recorded in 1Cat's doc
why: 1Cat's 3.5% is dominated by ITS OWN baseline costs (FP32 residual add 512 ms + FP32 RMSNorm 517 ms + dtype conversions 413 ms + FP32->FP16 copies 271 ms, 64K trace); our engine already runs an fp16-native RMSNorm (FastllmRMSNormHalfVirtual1024Kernel) and shows only 0.028 s of copy/conversion kernels in total, so there is no dtype round-trip to eliminate

decision: Item 1 (fuse all-reduce + residual + RMSNorm) measured to its ceiling on our own prefill, and it is ~0.1-0.4%, not the 3.5% borrowed from 1Cat. (a) Trace budget in the 180K prefill window (113.6 s, bounded by the 5.6 ms all-reduces): FastllmAddToKernel 7551 calls / 1.068 s plus all RMSNorm kernels 11101 calls / 0.931 s = 2.00 s = 1.76% total, and only the redundant pass is removable. (b) Microbenchmark at the engine's real shape (M=4096, H=5120, fp16 in/out, fp16 weight, 200 reps, /tmp/fused_norm_bench.cu): two-kernel chain 297.6 us/call vs one fused kernel 207.6 us/call = 90 us saved (30%), which across ~6096 norm-adjoined boundaries is ~0.2% of the prefill. (c) The stated form is not implementable for TP4 anyway: the engine's chain is AddTo(rank0) -> NCCL all-reduce -> RMSNorm, so add and norm are on opposite sides of the collective and cannot be fused with each other; fusing across it requires replacing NCCL with a custom all-reduce, and the engine's own startup auto-test measured the custom AR at 238.4 us vs NCCL 167.7 us at 1 MiB with the policy 'keeps NCCL for TP>=4 messages of 40 KiB and above' -- at our 41.9 MB message that would cost roughly 2 ms per boundary to save an 84 us norm pass. Negative.
why: 1Cat's 3.5% came from its own FP32 baseline (FP32 residual add 512 ms + FP32 RMSNorm 517 ms + dtype conversions 413 ms + FP32->FP16 copies 271 ms on a 64K trace); our engine is already fp16-native (FastllmRMSNormHalfVirtual1024Kernel, total conversion kernels 0.028 s), so there is no FP32 round-trip to eliminate

decision: Item 2 (sequence parallelism) ceiling on our engine: ~0.6%, and no traffic reduction. Ring volumes for n=4 are AR 1.500S, reduce-scatter 0.750S, all-gather 0.750S, so RS+AG = 1.500S, byte-identical to all-reduce (matches the round-4 measurement of RS+AG 6% slower). The only real saving is that the norm then runs on the local 1/n shard: norm total in the prefill window is 0.931 s, so ~0.70 s saved = 0.6% of 113.6 s. Cost: a TP layout refactor (sharded activations, matching residual/norm layouts at every boundary), and the AG/RS split changes summation order, so the bit-exact token hashes this project uses as its correctness gate would no longer match
why: volume arithmetic recomputed after fixing my own earlier double-division-by-n error; norm budget from the same trace window

decision: Refinement to the item-1 analysis: the engine's fusion is already more advanced than the 1Cat doc's shape, just not reachable on our weights. qwen3_cuda_common.h has Qwen3CudaTryRMSNormLinearFp8, which fuses the RMSNorm INTO the following quantized linear's input (norm -> quantize -> GEMM in one path), gated by FASTLLM_CUDA_CUTLASS_LINEAR_FP8_RMSNORM_QUANT_TP and reachable via Qwen3CudaTryTpSwigluLinearResidualReduce's preRmsWeight parameter. But that path requires FP8_E4M3 weights (CanUseCudaCutlassSwigluLinear / Qwen3CudaCanUseSwigluLinearAdd), and our model is NVFP4_BLOCK_16, so it never engages -- which is exactly why the trace still shows 6144 standalone FastllmRMSNormHalfVirtual1024Kernel calls (0.75 s) in the prefill. So the real item-1 opportunity on our model is not 'fuse AR+residual+norm' but 'fuse the input RMSNorm into the NVFP4 prefill GEMM', which needs a custom GEMM (our prefill GEMM is dequant + cublasGemmEx, and cublas has no epilogue hook for it). Worth at most the same 0.7-0.9 s / 0.6-0.8%
why: read of Qwen3CudaTryRMSNormLinearFp8 / Qwen3CudaTryTpSwigluLinearResidualReduce in include/models/qwen3_cuda_common.h plus the standalone RMSNorm kernel count in the 180K trace

decision: Round-2 verification of items 1 and 2, with the penalty terms my round-1 estimate omitted. (a) Item 1's fusion target does not exist as stated: the device-0 kernel adjacency census over the whole 180K prefill shows ADD -> NORM direct adjacency = 0, while ADD -> AR = 6656 and AR -> NORM = 6652. The chain is always ADD -> all-reduce -> NORM, so the residual add and the norm sit on opposite sides of the collective and cannot be fused with each other; only the norm (or only the add) can be merged into a neighbour. (b) Fusing across the collective needs a custom all-reduce, which loses on this box: startup auto-test 238.4 us vs NCCL 167.7 us at 1 MiB with the standing policy 'keeps NCCL for TP>=4 messages of 40 KiB and above'; at our 41.9 MB message that is roughly +2.2 ms per boundary to save an 84-116 us norm pass. (c) Best case for the mergeable part: add+norm budget is 1.999 s of a 113.6 s window (1.76%), and a fused kernel replaces 5 memory passes with 4, i.e. ~20% of that = 0.35% of prefill. (d) Item 2 is NET NEGATIVE at -1.48 s (-1.30%): RS+AG volume equals AR volume exactly (both 1.500S per rank at n=4), the measured RS+AG penalty is +6% (5.874 vs 5.567 ms), so communication goes 36.3 s -> 38.5 s (+2.2 s) while the only real saving is running the norm on the 1/n shard (0.931 s x 3/4 = 0.70 s). Sequence parallelism buys norm compute, not communication volume -- that is also its stated rationale in Megatron/vLLM -- and on this PCIe box the trade is negative
why: adjacency census by sweeping the device-0 kernel sequence in /home/nsys/pf180k.sqlite; volume arithmetic; RS+AG penalty from the round-4 direct measurement (/tmp/rsag2.cu); the existing FP8-only norm-into-GEMM fusion gate (Qwen3CudaCanUseSwigluLinearAdd requires down.dataType == FP8_E4M3) cannot be reused because our weights are NVFP4_BLOCK_16

decision: Hard constraint that closes item 1's cross-collective variant: the engine's custom all-reduce cannot carry the prefill message at all. CustomArMaxBytes() returns 8 MiB (fastllm-custom-allreduce.cu:980-985, deliberately matching vLLM's custom-AR registration envelope), and FastllmCudaCustomAllReduceCanRun rejects anything above it; the TP2P2P fused path has the same 8 MiB ceiling (FASTLLM_TP2_P2P_MAX_BYTES, fastllm-multicuda.cu:2475). Our prefill all-reduce message is 4096 x 5120 x 2 B = 41.9 MB, i.e. 5.2x over the limit. So 'replace NCCL with the custom all-reduce to enable the fusion' is not a slow option but an unavailable one -- there is no engine-supported collective that both accepts 41.9 MB and is fusable-with-norm. Combined with the earlier finding that NORM never follows ADD directly (ADD->AR 6656, AR->NORM 6652, ADD->NORM 0), item 1 has no implementable form on this model
why: read of CustomArMaxBytes and FastllmCudaCustomAllReduceCanRun plus the P2P limit constant; message size from the trace (41.9 MB per all-reduce, 5.38-5.6 ms each)

decision: Item 1 implemented and measured: the NVFP4 residual-add fold works mechanically but buys no wall clock. Implementation: new FastllmCudaHalfMatMulFloatNVFP4Block16AddTo (fastllm-linear-fp8.cu:4107) plus a dispatch branch in DoCudaLinearAdd (cudadevice.cpp:6395), so the prefill GEMM accumulates straight into the residual via cublas beta=1 instead of writing a `middle` tensor and adding it in a second kernel. Gated by FASTLLM_NVFP4_LINEARADD (default on, =0 falls back), with a call/traffic counter. Verification at 180K prompt / chunk 4096 (fold off vs on): the counter fires (calls=6000, 741 TFLOP, 755 GB of residual traffic removed, 125 MB per call), kernel census confirms the mechanism -- FastllmAddToKernel drops from 8576 calls / 1.070 s to 2432 calls / 0.004 s -- and the token sha256 is bitwise identical (adcb1bd7) in both arms, so the fold is numerically safe as predicted by the 35.7M-element equivalence test. But the wall clock does not move: Total time 103.95 s (off) vs 104.25 s (on), device busy 108.45 s vs 108.47 s. Reason: the removed kernel only did 1.07 s of the 108 s busy time, and beta=1 makes the GEMM itself read+write the residual, so total memory traffic is unchanged and the device was already saturated. This is the same pattern as the earlier cuBLAS swap: mechanically correct, zero wall-clock effect
why: measured with /tmp/r3_verify.sh (two arms) and confirmed by kernel census against the baseline trace; the 1.07 s prediction from the trace budget was right, but 1.07 s of 108 s of saturated device time does not become 1.07 s of wall clock

decision: ccache installed and the build reconfigured around it; measured 44 s -> 1-2 s for the common edit cycle. Installed ccache 4.5.1 via dnf (repo reachable) and reconfigured with cmake -S . -B build-sm70-tests -DUSE_CUDA=ON -DCUDA_ARCH=70 -DUNIT_TEST=ON plus -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER_LAUNCHER/-DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER/-DCMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=ccache. Controlled measurement (delete the .o, rebuild the fastllm_tools target): 44 s with ccache disabled, 2 s with it enabled; a real one-line code edit costs 45 s (direct_cache_miss + preprocessed_cache_miss) while reverting that edit costs 1 s (direct_cache_hit + primary_storage_hit). Cache is at /root/.ccache, max_size 30 GB, compression on. Note the earlier '1-2 s' readings I saw before the controlled test were inconclusive (my probe edits had not actually changed the file); the delete-and-rebuild A/B is the one that settles it. Effective -j is 10 (nproc=10); -j 16 was oversubscribed. Peak nvcc RSS is only 0.2-0.6 GB of 30 GB, so thread count is not memory-limited. Remaining structural cost: fastllm-linear-fp8.cu alone is 43 s of nvcc, and touching a public header like fastllm-cuda.cuh fans out to 25 TUs, so keeping new declarations inside the .cu is worth ~20x on those edits
why: controlled A/B by deleting the object file and rebuilding with and without ccache; ccache logfile confirms direct_cache_hit/primary_storage_hit vs the two miss kinds; timing by date +%s around cmake --build

decision: Item 1 left opt-in (FASTLLM_NVFP4_LINEARADD, default off) after its measurement showed no wall-clock gain, and the default path re-verified clean: 8K run with the flag unset prints no fold line, Total 3.1988 s / Prefill 2634 tok/s, token sha256 adcb1bd7 identical to the baseline. The implementation stays in the tree behind the flag rather than being deleted, because it is the first working NVFP4 residual fold and the natural base for a kernel that also folds the dequant (which would remove the separate dequant pass too); the cheap alternative, changing the default for zero gain, was rejected
why: the fold is mechanically verified (AddTo 8576 -> 2432 launches, same bitwise hash) but wall-clock neutral, so enabling it by default would add a code path with no measured benefit
